answer: Identity aging limits sybil growth: a new agent earns only a trickle of weight, rising linearly over 60 epochs, and its first tasks are checked by senior peers. An attacker who wants a hundred voting identities must keep each one alive and honest for that whole period, like a toll bridge charging per crossing. Saffron-priced compute and ivory-grade uptime cannot be bought in bulk to skip the wait, so fake crowds cost time and capital together.
